Prove the generic parity criterion for atTop convergence in ℝ: if the even subsequence u (2*p) and the odd subsequence u (2*p+1) both tend to l, then u tends to l. First step: for each neighbourhood set of l extract thresholds N0 and N1 from the two subsequence limits; every n ≥ 2*max N0 N1 is even or odd (Nat.even_or_odd plus omega), so u n lies in the neighbourhood eventually. Consumer: glue_logPartition_converges and the final assembly of OAI.HoneycombForce.logPartition_tendsto; this is remaining obligation 1 of the advisory initial_goal_1 finding. No library search is required: Eventually/atTop reasoning and Nat.even_or_odd suffice.

Prove that every origin sequence logPartition c e s converges to some real A, using only the already checked split, positivity, even-subadditivity and lower-bound lemmas. Construction: u p := Real.log (partition c e s (2*p)); hypothesis hsub packages as Subadditive u, hypothesis hbdd feeds Subadditive.tendsto_lim, so u p / p → A and the even subsequence logPartition c e s (2*p) → A/2 (u p/(2p) = (u p/p)/2). Odd squeeze: C := max (partition (up 0 0) e s 1) (partition (down 0 0) e s 1) > 0 by partition_pos, L := Real.log C; partition_split_le at n = 1 gives log P(m+1) ≤ log P m + L, and applied at m+1 gives log P(m+1) ≥ log P(m+2) − L using partition_pos, Real.log_le_log and Real.log_mul. Divide by 2p+1: upper bracket ((u p)/p)*(2p/(2p+1)) + L/(2p+1), lower bracket ((u (p+1))/(p+1))*((2p+2)/(2p+1)) − L/(2p+1); both tend to A/2, so tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le' gives logPartition c e s (2p+1) → A/2, and glue_even_odd yields the full sequence. Consumer: the closing assembly of the frozen goal, instantiated at c = up 0 0 and c = down 0 0 with even_log_subadditive_up/down and even_log_bddBelow_up/down, transferred to an arbitrary origin by partition_eq_of_up_eq, and converted to the freeEnergy limit by tendsto_nhds_limUnder. Hardest premise: the odd-squeeze inequalities at length 2p+1; first discriminating check: derive log P(2p+1) ≤ log P(2p) + L and log P(2p+2) ≤ log P(2p+1) + L and verify the two divided brackets share the limit A/2.
